entry.title: When a standing child resists lying down for a change
entry.summary: For a child who already pulls up to standing and resists lying down, the authors describe a standing diaper change with the adult seated low. Their emphasis remains gentle, private care and participation.
entry.cue: Your child already pulls up and wants to stay standing when a diaper needs changing.
detail: In the home chapter, the adult sits on a low stool while the child stands for the change, if the space allows. The later diapering chapter connects this possibility with a child who may feel vulnerable when laid down.

The adult still explains what is happening and provides the cleaning. For a bowel movement, the book’s example has the child lean forward with their hands on the side of the bathtub; the same passage describes front-to-back wiping.

The authors keep other possibilities in view: a wish to finish playing, choose something or take more of a part. A standing change does not explain every protest. If necessary care still meets resistance, they describe acknowledging the child’s feelings and proceeding with gentle hands.
